headline: Boreal Wilderness Camping and Hiking Permits
reservation: Front-country camping at Hattie Cove can be reserved online, while backcountry hiking on the Coastal Trail requires a separate permit and safety orientation. Reservation systems typically open in early spring; always check the Parks Canada site for the current year's exact launch date.

days.title: Hattie Cove and Southern Headland

stops.name: Manito Miikana Trail
stops.detail: Climb the rocky ridges for a panoramic view of Lake Superior and the Pic River dunes.

stops.name: Horseshoe Bay
stops.detail: Visit the sheltered sandy beach to see the contrast between the calm cove and the rough open waters of the lake.

days.driving: Allow 30–45 minutes from Marathon to the Hattie Cove gate; road conditions can vary with weather.
days.note: Trails involve rugged Canadian Shield terrain; steady footwork is required.

days.title: Suspension Bridge Wilderness Trek

stops.name: White River Suspension Bridge
stops.detail: Hike through the boreal forest to cross a 23-meter high bridge over the Chigamiwinigum Falls.

stops.name: White River Vista
stops.detail: View the powerful river gorge from designated viewpoints along the bridge approach.

days.driving: No driving; this is a full-day out-and-back wilderness hike starting from the Hattie Cove trailhead.
days.note: This is a strenuous 18km round trip; allow 6–9 hours depending on personal pace.

days.title: Coastal Vistas and Cultural Landscapes

stops.name: Bimose Kinoomagewnan Trail
stops.detail: Learn about the Anishinaabe culture through interpretive signage surrounding Halfway Lake.

stops.name: Middle Beach
stops.detail: Observe the massive driftwood logs deposited by Superior's storms on this expansive cobble and sand beach.

days.driving: Short drives between Hattie Cove trailheads; allow for gravel road sections.
days.note: Black bears are common in this region; utilize the bear-proof storage provided at all sites.

intel.title: Hattie Cove Lots
intel.text: Primary parking is available at the Visitor Centre and the Coastal Trailhead. Space is usually sufficient for the low-density visitor volume, though peak weekends may see fuller lots.

intel.title: Wilderness Connectivity
intel.text: Cellular service is extremely limited and generally non-existent once you leave the Hattie Cove developed area. Travelers should carry a satellite communication device for backcountry travel.

intel.title: Marathon Supply Hub
intel.text: Marathon is the last reliable stop for fuel, groceries, and hardware before entering the park. No commercial services exist within Pukaskwa National Park boundaries.

intel.title: Seasonal Operation
intel.text: Full services are typically available from June to September. Outside of this window, the road may be gated or unmaintained, requiring self-reliance.

intel.title: Hwy 627 Approach
intel.text: The park is accessed via Highway 627, which is a paved but winding road through dense forest. Watch for moose and other wildlife, particularly during dawn and dusk hours.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental at Sault Ste. Marie Airport, then drive roughly 5 hours north on Highway 17. Stop in Marathon for all supplies before the final leg.
plan.vehicle: Reliable vehicles with high clearance are preferred for the region; check rental contracts for restrictions on unpaved park access roads.
plan.goldenHour: Horseshoe Bay for sunset; the westward facing Lake Superior vistas are season-dependent and often dramatic.
